newsitem.title: USA: U.S. PRODUCTS OUTLOOK-GASOLINE BUYERS BACKING OUT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. PRODUCTS OUTLOOK-GASOLINE BUYERS BACKING OUT.

text.p: U.S. spot gasoline markets are likely to see increased volatility in the coming week, as the summer gasoline buying interest showed signs of waning.
Meanwhile, distillate prices hovered inside the trading range that has limited movements since early May, traders said.
On the U.S. Gulf, prompt conventional M1 gasoline prices sat at about 61.70 cents a gallon at the end of last week, off the high of 65.50 cents reached earlier in the week.
"Frankly, you've got a lot of fear when the numbers get high. The longs get scared and start to dump it," one spot market player said.
That weakness was evident on the Colonial Pipeline's scheduling deadline for the M1's front 23rd cycle last week, traders said.

Differentials for that material on the Houston-to-New York Harbor line fell more than 1.00 cent on the final day as bullish traders were forced to chase buyers to lower levels, indicating that many players had already covered their supply commitments.
"I think you'll probably see people selling pretty hard -- at least until was get another supply shortage. It will probably be very volatile this week," the trader said.
Overall U.S. gasoline demand sat at 7.955 million barrels a day, up 1.5 percent from the year-ago level of 7.838 million barrels, according to Energy Information Administration figures.

But that steady offtake has been nearly matched by the heavy output from U.S. refineries, which kicked out nearly 7.8 million barrels a day of gasoline for the week end Aug. 1, according to the American Petroleum Institute data.
Traders said they expected differentials for gasoline in New York Harbor to weaken as supply pressure on prompt barrels eases amid fresh imports and a declining number of buyers.
On Monday, the market opened to a covey of aggressive sellers on the lookout for buyers.
"Differentials are weaker because people are realizing there are imports from Europe and the Caribbean coming in," said a Harbor trader.
By late last week, differentials showed signs of slackening as buyers disappeared from play, and supply pressure on prompt barrels eased.
"Gasoline is still fairly strong and pretty backwardated as you go further out in the month" but the spread with October gasoline has come off, said a Harbor trader.
On Monday, prompt M2 unleaded conventional northern-grade gasoline fell a half cent to put offers at 4.50 cents over the print, with the buyers hard to find.
It was unclear, however, if the decline on gasoline would translate into greater interest on heating oil, which soon begins its traditional stock building period.
But players have said many buyers have already stocked up on supply, taking advantage of the low values seen this spring.
In the Midcontinent, gasoline differentials were expected to continue easing although demand remained healthy.
"The market got pretty hyped up earlier and we've been drifting down from that," said a Group Three player.
Both the Group and Chicago markets skyrocketed two weeks following production glitches in the Midwest. The markets began to ease early last week.
On Monday, Group Three was down a penny at 3.75/4.00 cents a gallon, with Chicago unleaded down a half cent at 3.00/3.25 cents.
-- Matt Daily and Laney Salisbury, New York Oil Desk
